correctness.rationale: The seven vertices are exactly the nonzero proper divisor ideals, and adjacency is equivalent to both exponent sums being at least two. Explicit chronological forces prove Z<=2; degree four excludes a path and hence Z=1. A listed path decomposition has width two and an induced C4 forces treewidth at least two, giving tw=pw=2. The packaged deterministic checker exhausts all 128 subsets and returns coefficients 4,24,33,21,7,1.

originality.rationale: The closest algebra-primary source classifies small independence number but has no zero forcing or width treatment. The exact Z_n annihilating-ideal source proves weak perfectness and divisor structure. General zero forcing polynomial sources provide the invariant and standard families but no exact table for this graph. A graph-statistics database can cover the scalar zero forcing number, so novelty is assessed on the complete polynomial, minimum-set classification, arithmetic realization, and width certificates.
residual_risks: An isomorphic unlabeled seven-vertex graph may have its complete zero forcing polynomial tabulated in an unindexed source.
Generic graph databases can already compute the scalar zero forcing number.
The finding is a complete classification of one natural exponent pattern, not a formula for arbitrary p^a q^b.
The prime values themselves are invisible to the graph.

value.rationale: The p^2q^2 case is the smallest balanced nonreduced two-factor annihilating-ideal graph and sits at the independence-four boundary studied in algebra-primary literature. Its mixed triangle/four-cycle structure falls outside elementary path, tree, complete multipartite, and threshold families. The exact forcing polynomial, all minimizers, and width-two certificates form a motivated benchmark for the general two-prime-power exponent grid rather than an arbitrary induced subgraph calculation.
